children: Unveiled on day 2 of Singapore FinTech Festival (SFF) 2026, Visa Recurrent is a next-generation subscription management solution that gives consumers greater visibility and control while helping financial institutions and merchants reduce friction across the recurring payment lifecycle
Kiwibank, the largest New Zealand owned bank, is the first issuer globally to bring Visa Recurrent directly into its mobile banking app and internet banking

SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Visa, a world leader in digital payments, today announced Visa Recurrent, a new solution that connects consumers, financial institutions and participating merchants across the recurring payments lifecycle. It enables consumers to view and manage recurring payments through their financial institution's digital banking experiences, giving them greater visibility and control over recurring payments, at the same time helping financial institutions and merchants deliver more seamless payment experiences.

Visa also announced that Kiwibank is the first issuer globally to deploy Visa Recurrent through its mobile banking app and internet banking, to help give Kiwibank customers a simpler way to understand and manage recurring payments commitments on a channel they already use and trust.
"At Kiwibank, we're always looking for practical ways to make managing money easier," said
Mark Stephen, Chief Customer Officer – Retail at Kiwibank

. "We're proud to work with Visa to bring this capability to our Kiwi customers first. It's an exciting milestone and a great example of what can be achieved when organisations work together with a clear focus on customer outcomes."
Meet Visa Recurrent: More Control, Less Hassle

From streaming and fitness memberships to software and household bills, recurring payments have become a part of everyday life. Yet managing those commitments can still require navigating multiple websites, apps, and customer-service channels. Through participating financial institutions, Visa Recurrent enables consumers to access a consolidated view of eligible recurring payments and take supported actions directly within their digital banking experience.

For participating merchants, Visa Recurrent creates a more connected way to manage customer relationships throughout the recurring payment lifecycle. When consumers take supported actions through their financial institution, merchants may receive timely notifications and use redirects to engage the customer directly.
"Consumers shouldn't have to hunt across websites, apps and customer service channels just to understand or manage their subscriptions," said
T.R. Ramachandran, Head of Products and Solutions, Asia Pacific, Visa

. "Visa Recurrent helps financial institutions bring that visibility and control into the digital banking experiences consumers already use and trust. This makes recurring payments easier to manage while giving banks another way to strengthen their everyday relationship with customers."
Built for the Way People Pay Today

Consumers increasingly expect simple ways to manage recurring payments, while merchants and financial institutions need clearer signals to manage those relationships efficiently. According to Visa research[1], one in three New Zealand consumers say they've continued paying for a service they no longer use, and 86% want their bank to provide tools that help them manage recurring payments. Visa Recurrent responds to that demand by enabling participating financial institutions to provide a more connected management experience through their existing digital channels.

Beginning today, Visa Recurrent will be available to participating financial institutions in Asia Pacific. Visa Recurrent is the latest evolution in a full suite in subscription management solutions from Visa, including Visa Stop Payment Service and Visa Subscription Manager. Learn more at visa.com.
